newsitem.title: MONACO: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN ON POLE FOR MONACO GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN ON POLE FOR MONACO GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany ended his Williams team mate Jacques Villeneuve's run of five pole positions on Saturday when he claimed the prime starting place for Sunday's Monaco Grand Prix.
Frentzen, winner of the San Marino Grand Prix two week ago, clocked a fastest time of one minute 18.216 seconds to edge out compatriot Michael Schumacher in a Ferrari by 0.019 seconds.

The double world champion, who had been fastest for most of the session, made a tremendous bid to regain pole in the final minutes but had to settle for second best on an all-German front row for the 55th running of the classic race.
World championship leading Canadian Villeneuve was third fastest in his Williams and will share the second row of the grid with Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan.
Frentzen's pole was the first of his career and came in his 53rd Grand Prix.
